question: Can the company's voice on X be held to two rules it cannot break — every claim checked against a committed receipt, and nothing leaving without Simon's approval of those exact words — while it runs key-ready, so that on the day Simon authorises the connector nothing about it changes?
why: Simon's AI-first company spec (2026-10-28), build step 2: 'the OAuth posting connector under Kar's claim gate'. Hard lines: never handle OAuth secrets (the connector is dry-run until Simon authorises it himself); nothing posted, sent, replied or DM'd without Simon's explicit approval in chat for that action; the claim gate checks every claim against a committed receipt. kar-voice already drafts from receipt cards, gates length/duplicates/daily cap, replies only when summoned, and signs OAuth 1.0a — but its `post` would post the oldest queued draft with no approval, and a card's claim is free text checked against nothing.

design.card: A card names its receipt by repo (sjgant80-hub/<name>), full 40-hex commit, path to one JSON file, and that file's sha256; and lists facts: {path, value} — dotted paths into the receipt and the value each must have there.
design.claimGate: The IO fetches the receipt from GitHub at the pinned commit and hashes it; the kernel refuses the card if: the receipt is not pinned to a full commit; the hash differs; a fact's path is missing or holds another value; a fact sits inside a claim that FAILED (an object on its path with held:false or pass:false); any number in the post's name or claim is not one of the facts' numbers (whole numbers exactly, decimals rounded to the places the post shows, a percentage as the field x100); the post has a hype word, a price, an economy term or estate jargon; the link leaves the estate's own pages and repos.
design.approval: An approval record names the item and the sha256 of its exact text: { itemId, textSha256, by: 'simon' | 'rehearsal', via: 'chat', quote, at }. Kar writes a 'simon' record only on Simon's word in chat, quoting it. A 'rehearsal' record (the demo's) can only ever authorise a dry run. A later { itemId, withdrawn: true } cancels it. `post` refuses anything without a matching approval, re-runs the claim gate at post time, and calls X only with the owner's keys present AND DRY_RUN=0.

forgeryRule.note: Seven forgeries from each genuine card, made mechanically; each must be refused, and for its own reason (the reason text must contain the marker).

F1.make: in the claim, the last digit of the first number becomes (digit+1) mod 10
F1.marker: is not a field of the receipt

F2.make: F1, and every fact whose value is a number equal to the original number is set to the new number

F3.make: the first hex character of the pinned sha256 becomes the next one (f to 0)
F3.marker: not the file the card pinned

F5.make: the claim is prefixed 'the best result yet: '

F6.make: the claim is suffixed ' — from £49 a month'

F7.make: the claim is suffixed ' — and earn KCC on every run'

claims.claim: Nothing goes out without Simon's approval of the exact words. In a sandbox with X replaced by a recorder and fake keys: no approval -> X called 0 times; approved then edited by one character -> 0; a rehearsal approval in live mode -> 0; approval withdrawn -> 0; Simon's approval in a dry run -> 0 calls and one dry-run record of exactly the approved text; Simon's approval in live mode -> exactly 1 call, carrying exactly the approved text.
The keys never surface: with fake key values in the environment through every V5 run, nothing the organ writes to its files or prints contains any of them.

scope: The gate checks that every number is the receipt's number at a named field, that the receipt is the committed one, and that the claim it cites held. It cannot check that the words around a number describe it fairly — that is what Simon's approval of the exact text is for. The approval record is Kar's record of Simon's word in chat, quoted; it is not a signature by Simon.
